description: We are Team ASTRIONYX, participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project aims to develop health monitoring software for astronauts to visualize health data and identify potential health concerns during space missions. We welcome passionate team members interested in space science, programming, healthcare technology, data analysis, and UI/UX design. Beginners are welcome!
summary:
ASTROCARE is a software-based astronaut health monitoring and analysis prototype developed to demonstrate how astronaut health information can be monitored, visualized, and analyzed during space missions.

The system integrates simulated live health monitoring, AI-based anomaly detection, sleep tracking, mental wellness monitoring, and historical blood serum data analysis into a single interactive dashboard.

It allows users to monitor multiple astronaut profiles, observe changes in health parameters, identify unusual readings using machine learning, and analyze historical blood measurements obtained from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).

ASTROCARE aims to demonstrate how different health information sources can be brought together to support astronaut health awareness and mission health management. It provides an accessible prototype that can be further developed to integrate real-time sensors and advanced health analysis systems in the future.
details:
ASTROCARE is an integrated astronaut health monitoring and analysis prototype designed to demonstrate how multiple health-related parameters can be observed and analyzed through a single software platform.

During long-duration space missions, astronauts may experience changes in physical health, sleep patterns, stress levels, and other physiological conditions. Monitoring these different aspects is important for understanding astronaut well-being and supporting mission health management.

ASTROCARE addresses this concept through the following modules:

1. Live Astronaut Health Monitoring

The application provides simulated health readings for multiple astronaut profiles. It displays important parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and stress level.

Users can start and stop monitoring and observe how the readings change over time. Each astronaut profile maintains its own health history.

2. AI-Based Anomaly Detection

ASTROCARE uses the Isolation Forest machine learning algorithm to identify unusual patterns in the collected health readings.

The system analyzes the available readings and flags observations that differ from the expected pattern. This feature demonstrates how machine learning can support the identification of unusual health data.

3. Sleep Monitoring

The sleep monitoring module records illustrative sleep information and displays sleep duration, sleep history, and related trends.

It also provides visualizations to explore the relationship between sleep and other recorded parameters.

4. Mental Wellness Monitoring

The mental wellness module allows users to record mood and stress information. This provides an additional perspective on astronaut well-being beyond physical health measurements.

5. NASA Historical Blood Serum Analysis

ASTROCARE integrates historical blood serum data from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), using the OSD-575 study dataset.

Users can select available blood parameters and examine their measurements through graphs and tables. The system also compares measurements with the reference ranges available in the dataset.

6. Participant Historical Comparison

The application provides a facility to compare historical blood measurements from different participants, helping users explore variations in the available research data.

7. Health Trends and Reports

The dashboard displays health trends through interactive visualizations. Users can also download health information in CSV format and generate PDF health reports.

Technology Used

  • Programming language: Python
  • Dashboard framework: Streamlit
  • Data processing: Pandas and NumPy
  • Data visualization: Plotly
  • Machine learning: Scikit-learn
  • PDF report generation: ReportLab
  • Historical research data: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR)

Expected Benefits and Future Scope

ASTROCARE demonstrates how simulated health monitoring, machine learning, historical research data, and data visualization can be integrated into one platform.

In the future, the prototype could be expanded to support real-time sensor integration, more advanced health analytics, additional NASA datasets, and improved astronaut health trend analysis.

Important limitation: ASTROCARE is currently a prototype. Its live readings are simulated, its sleep information is illustrative, and its blood analysis uses historical research data. It is not connected to real astronaut sensors and is not a medical device or a diagnostic system
